newsitem.title: JAPAN: Argentina minister sees annual GDP growth of 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina minister sees annual GDP growth of 5 pct.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Monday that his country may post an annual economic growth rate of about five percent on average over the next 10 to 20 years.
Fernandez told a news conference in Tokyo that Argentina will be able to achieve gross domestic product (GDP) growth of more than five percent in 1997.
"I see robust economic growth in the mid- to long-term and we may be able to achieve annual growth of about five percent over the next 10 to 20 years," he said.
He also said he hopes Argentina's unemployment rate will be reduced to 15 percent in 1997 from 17.4 percent in 1996.
Fernandez is in Tokyo to attend an annual meeting of Japanese and Argentine companies.
Asked whether Argentina has plans to issue more yen-denominated bonds, Fernandez said that the government is considering that possibility. He said it was premature to give any details.
Argentina has issued 50 billion yen worth of yen- denominated bonds over a six-year period, he said.
Argentina, which exports minerals and industrial goods to Japan, would like to add meat to that list, but has been unable to do so because of Japan's strict health standards, he said.
Since Argentina is already exporting about 20,000 tonnes of meat to the United States, it has been asking Japan to deregulate its sanitary standards, Fernandez said.
